hoy.titular: A week from the final, La Plata wakes up plastered with glory and Palmeiras miss out on the Brasileirão

foto.alt: Estudiantes' starting XI pose at the Maracanã before the semi-final against Flamengo.

hoy.resumen: The city's streets filled with posters bearing quotes from Zubeldía, Bilardo, Pachamé and Sabella, and Medina said the team play well when emotions run high. In São Paulo, Palmeiras drew 1-1 with several regulars and Flamengo were crowned champions of Brazil.

siete.titulo: Correa in the final stretch of his recovery
siete.texto: He remains a doubt with the tear in his right hamstring, but according to El Día he is in the final stage of his recovery. The plan is for him to start; if he is not fully fit, he could come on in the second half, which would open the door for Cetré.

siete.titulo: Without Baltasar, Medina likely to stick with a back five
siete.texto: Baltasar Rodríguez, sent off against Flamengo, will miss the final. According to El Día, the main option is to repeat the three centre-backs and two wing-backs used at the Maracanã, with Tobio Burgos on the left; Diario Hoy names Fabricio Pérez, who started in the Supercopa Argentina, as an alternative.

siete.titulo: Palmeiras draw and Flamengo are champions of Brazil
siete.texto: It finished 1-1 in São Paulo: Jhon Arias headed the opener and Samuel Lino equalised. Abel did not rest everyone: Gustavo Gómez, Andreas Pereira, Arias, Flaco López and Vitor Roque all played, while Murilo, Piquerez and Paulinho remain doubts for the final; on Tuesday 24th they visit Chapecoense.

siete.titulo: Around 35,000 Pincha fans head for Montevideo
siete.texto: 120 coaches are going: 60 laid on by the club, leaving the UNO on the afternoon of Friday 27th, and 60 from supporters' groups and branches. Friday and Saturday ferries are sold out, and 2009 champions invited by the club will also be at the Centenario.

siete.titulo: The road map to the Centenario
siete.texto: The squad trained this morning in City Bell and have Sunday off. They stay at the Country Club until Wednesday 25th, when they travel to Montevideo (staying at the Hilton); on Thursday and Friday they will train at Montevideo City Torque's training ground.
In an interview released by CONMEBOL, the Cacique said his side are very emotional and that, when emotions run high, they usually play well. "I believe a lot in this team", he added.

The streets woke up covered in posters with quotes from club legends: "You don't reach glory along a bed of roses" (Zubeldía), "Close your eyes and believe" (Sabella), "Go for glory" (Bilardo) and "Never give up" (Pachamé).

linea.texto: Palmeiras drew 1-1 with Flamengo, who are crowned Brasileirão champions.
"Close your eyes and believe": the poster campaign building up to the final on the streets.
La Plata's walls woke up plastered with Pincha legends.
Medina looks ahead to the final: "When our emotions are running high, we usually play well".
CONMEBOL build up the final with Flaco López and José Sosa.
Rojo and González Pirez, a week from the final: "We have the match of our lives ahead of us".
Estudiantes de la Patria: the final also breaks the Argentina-Brazil tie in the all-time standings.
Palmeiras set to rest starters against Flamengo: Murilo in transition, Piquerez and Paulinho in treatment.
CONMEBOL invites the youngest Pincha fans to draw the crest or the shirt for its social media.
A fan set off from La Plata by bike for the final in Montevideo.
The squad celebrated the Supercopa with an asado and a good atmosphere ahead of the final.
Paulinho still has no return date and is a doubt for Palmeiras in the final.
Palmeiras on alert: three key players nursing knocks days before the final.
Palmeiras hope to have Piquerez, Murilo and Paulinho back for the final.
